### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §6.2.1, Example 6.2 (printed p. 185; PDF p. 197; item `7sketches:6.2.1:example6.2`) states the colimit end of this identification at its smallest instance: in a preorder regarded as a thin category, an initial object is exactly a bottom element. That is the empty-family specialisation this issue's work already schedules ("specialise to binary products and to the empty family (top/bottom elements)"), read on the colimit side, so no new general theorem is demanded.

What Seven Sketches adds is the pair of concrete witnesses the book uses to make the point, neither of which exists in tree. `Instance/Proset.v:47` defines `LessThanEqualTo_Category := @Proset nat Nat.le _` and carries no `Initial` instance (nor does `Instance/Omega.v`'s `Omega`), so "0 is initial in (ℕ, ≤)" is unformalized; and the book's negative half — the reals under their usual order have no bottom element — has no carrier either, since the tree contains no real numbers at all. Phase-D verification also surfaced a witness Phase C missed: the walking arrow `_2` is a two-element preorder with a terminal but no initial instance, and `Construction/Enriched/Two.v:46`'s `two_bot` is precisely the bottom-element datum left unpackaged.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §6.2.1) An `Initial` instance for `Instance/Proset.v:47`'s `LessThanEqualTo_Category` exhibiting `0` as the bottom of (ℕ, ≤), and a preorder-with-no-bottom witness in the `@Initial C → False` form — the reals being unavailable, `Instance/Two/Discrete.v`'s two-element discrete order or `Construction/Enriched/Two.v:46`'s `two_bot` context is the in-tree substitute.

Phase-D note on the coverage record's wording: it originally claimed the library "has no way to state that a category has no initial object". That overreached — `@Initial C → False` is perfectly expressible; the library simply never writes it.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §6.2.1, Exercise 6.3 (printed p. 185; PDF p. 197; item `7sketches:6.2.1:ex6.3`) asks for three preorders on a two-element set: one whose category has no initial object, one with exactly one, and one with two. The middle case *is* this issue's `Initial` structure on `_2` — the two-element linear order whose bottom is initial — so that third of the exercise is already scheduled here and needs nothing further.

The other two cases are a distinct obligation and are **not** appended as prose: they are filed as their own issue (Seven Sketches 6.2.1, "Deciding initiality in small concrete categories"), which introduces the `@Initial C → False` idiom for the discrete two-element order and constructs the codiscrete two-element preorder — a carrier the tree lacks entirely, `Structure/Discrete.v:23-24` promising the codiscrete construction and never supplying it — in which both objects are initial.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §6.2.1, Exercise 6.7 (printed pp. 185–186; PDF pp. 197–198; item `7sketches:6.2.1:ex6.7`) returns to the rigs of Chapter 5 from the initial-object side. Part 1 asks the reader to complete the definition of a rig homomorphism (preservation of `1` and of multiplication alongside the additive clauses), which is exactly this issue's scheduled `RigHom` and the category `Rig` — "mirroring `Theory/Algebra/Monoid/Hom.v`'s `Mon`/`Mon_Forget` shape". Nothing new is demanded there.

Part 2 asserts that `Rig` has an initial object and asks which one it is (the naturals: every rig admits exactly one rig homomorphism from ℕ, sending `n` to the `n`-fold sum of `1`). That is a formalizable increment this issue's Definition of Done does not currently scope, and there is nothing near it in tree: the closest algebraic-category initial objects are `Algs_Initial` (`Instance/Comp.v:209`, the free algebra on the empty set for a signature *without* equations, so it cannot discharge a variety like rigs) and `CMon_Initial` (`Instance/CMon/Biproduct.v:154`, the trivial monoid).

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §6.2.1) `Initial Rig` — the naturals are initial in the category of rigs, with the unique homomorphism out of `Nat_Rig` constructed and its uniqueness proved.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §6.2.1, Remark 6.9 (printed p. 186; PDF p. 198; item `7sketches:6.2.1:remark6.9`) gives the licence for speaking of *the* initial object: objects satisfying a universal property are unique up to unique isomorphism, the isomorphism being supplied by the property itself. That is exactly the uniqueness-with-uniqueness-of-the-iso refinement this issue already schedules for `terminal_unique` / `initial_unique` / `zero_object_unique`.

One thing Seven Sketches makes visible that the Mac Lane framing does not: the *general* theorem is already proved in tree. `Structure/UniversalProperty.v:175` has `univ_property_unique_up_to_unique_iso (c d : C) (t : P c) (s : P d) : Unique (fun p : (c ≅ d) => univ_property_respects_iso c d p t ≈ s)` under `Context (H : IsUniversalProperty C P eqP)` (opened at `:104-106`). What blocks the initial/terminal instance is not the theorem but its hypothesis: `IsUniversalProperty` has exactly three instances in the whole tree — `LimitIsUniversalProperty` (`Structure/UniversalProperty/Limit.v:141`), `CartesianProductIsUniversalProperty` (`Structure/UniversalProperty/Cartesian.v:60`) and `UniversalArrowIsUniversalProperty` (`Structure/UniversalProperty/Universal/Arrow.v:61`) — and none is at initiality or terminality, which is the very case the remark uses as its illustration. `Structure/Limit/Terminal.v:33`'s `Terminal_Limit : Limit F ↔ @Terminal C` is the bridge that would supply it and is never composed with `LimitIsUniversalProperty`.

This issue's work section offers routing through the UniversalProperty machinery as one option among two; the following makes the route a tracked obligation rather than a choice, because it is what turns the general theorem into a usable one.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §6.2.1) An `IsUniversalProperty` instance at terminality (and hence, by duality, initiality), so `univ_property_unique_up_to_unique_iso` applies directly — and with it the repair of a dangling in-tree pointer: `Theory/Isomorphism.v:82-83` advertises `Structure/Terminal.v` as "the simplest instance" of that theorem, but `Structure/Terminal.v` is 129 lines that `Require` only `Category.Lib` and `Category.Theory.Category` and contains no such instance.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §6.2.1, Exercise 6.10 (printed p. 186; PDF p. 198; item `7sketches:6.2.1:ex6.10`) asks for the construction itself: given two initial objects of a category, build an isomorphism between them using only the universal property — the two unique maps in either direction, whose composites are identities by uniqueness. That is precisely this issue's `initial_unique`, and this issue's Definition of Done already scopes it (including the uniqueness of the connecting isomorphism), so no additional obligation is added.

Worth recording for whoever takes it on: the tree today has *nothing* comparable. The only textual hit for the claim is `Structure/Initial.v:36`, which states it inside the file's background essay ("Any two initial objects are isomorphic by a unique isomorphism") while the file's actual assertions are only `initial_obj`, `zero`, `zero_unique` and `zero_comp`. `Structure/ZeroObject.v:42`'s `zero_coincide` is the different claim that a chosen initial and a chosen terminal object agree, and its header at `:20-22` leans on the uniqueness fact in prose without proving it. The concrete uniqueness lemmas that do exist for other universal objects — `equalizer_unique` (`Structure/Equalizer/Fork.v:106`), `coequalizer_unique` (`Structure/Coequalizer.v:106`), `pullback_unique` (`Structure/Pullback.v:182`) — all conclude a bare `q1 ≅ q2` with no uniqueness-of-the-iso clause, so they are strictly weaker than what this issue delivers.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §6.2.2, Exercise 6.13 (printed p. 186; PDF p. 198; item `7sketches:6.2.2:ex6.13`) asks why coproducts in a preorder coincide with joins. That is the dual half this issue already schedules — "dually for colimits and least upper bounds", specialised to binary coproducts — and this issue's `proset_colimit_iff_lub` is the exact statement, so no new obligation is added.

The in-tree situation confirms the sizing. There is one worked preorder and no general theorem: `Instance/Props.v:80` `Props_Cocartesian` computes the coproduct in the thin category `Props` (`:39`, `hom := Basics.impl` with every hom-setoid equivalence `True`) to be `or`, with injections `or_introl`/`or_intror` and copairing by case analysis — a genuine preorder whose coproduct is the join, and precisely one of the two "existing binary witnesses" this issue's work section proposes to record as instances. `Instance/Proset.v:33` builds the thin category of an arbitrary preorder and carries no `Cocartesian` (nor `Cartesian`, `Initial` or `Terminal`) instance, and no join/least-upper-bound notion is defined anywhere in the tree — every occurrence of "lattice", "Heyting" or "join" in that sense is header prose, e.g. `Instance/Poset.v:51`.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §6.2.2, Exercise 6.18 (printed p. 187; PDF pp. 199–200; item `7sketches:6.2.2:ex6.18`) develops the same construction as an exercise: from binary coproducts and an initial object, assemble the monoidal structure with `+` as tensor and the initial object as unit. Its parts (2) and (3) — the unitors `A + 0 ≅ A` and `0 + A ≅ A` and the associator `(A + B) + C ≅ A + (B + C)` — are exactly the components this issue assembles, and every one of them is already proved in tree as an `Isomorphism` instance: `coprod_zero_l` (`Structure/Cocartesian.v:375`), `coprod_zero_r` (`:384`), `coprod_assoc` (`:399`). The exercise's part (1), the action of `+` on morphisms, is the `cover`/`cover_id`/`cover_comp` triple (`Structure/Cocartesian.v:151`, `:285`, `:291`) and its packaging as a bifunctor is filed separately on #658. So the missing work really is the packaging, not new mathematics — the exercise itself stops short of the coherence axioms.

One piece of the exercise falls outside this issue's current Definition of Done. Exercise 6.18 asks for the **symmetry** `A + B → B + A` as well, and for it to be checked invertible, since its target (Definition 4.45) is a *symmetric* monoidal category. `coprod_comm` (`Structure/Cocartesian.v:393`, with `paws_invol` at `:279`) supplies the morphism and its invertibility, but nothing assembles it into a braided or symmetric structure, and the cartesian mirror that this issue dualizes does have one (`CC_SymmetricMonoidal`, `Structure/Monoidal/Internal/Product.v:314`, surfaced as `Cartesian_Monoidal` at `Structure/Monoidal/Cartesian.v:49`).

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §6.2.2) The braided and symmetric upgrades `Cocartesian_BraidedMonoidal` and `Cocartesian_SymmetricMonoidal`, with the braiding built from `coprod_comm` and the hexagon discharged — dual to `CC_SymmetricMonoidal`.

Context note for the implementer: `Instance/FinSet.v:29-31` states the consequence of this gap explicitly of its own coproduct-induced monoidal structure — "That monoidal assembly, and the [PROP] instance riding on it, need the coherence machinery and are not yet built" — and the only coproduct-tensor monoidal categories currently in tree live on `Cospan(C)`/`DecoratedCospan(C)`, not on `C` itself.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §6.2.2, Exercise 6.18 part (1) (printed p. 187; PDF pp. 199–200; item `7sketches:6.2.2:ex6.18`) asks the reader to show that binary coproduct extends to a functor `C × C → C` and to say how it acts on morphisms. That is exactly this issue's `InternalCoproductFunctor`, with the arrow action `cover` and the laws `cover_id`/`cover_comp`/`cover_respects` this issue already names — nothing further is demanded, and the Definition of Done here already scopes it.

The remaining parts of Exercise 6.18 — the unitors, the associator, the symmetry, and the assembly into a symmetric monoidal structure on `(C, +, 0)` — are recorded on #490.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §6.2.3, Example 6.22 (printed p. 189; PDF p. 201; item `7sketches:6.2.3:example6.22`) observes that in a preorder the pushout of a span `B ← A → C` is the coproduct of `B` and `C`, both being the join `B ∨ C` — so pushouts and coproducts coincide there. The join half is this issue's `proset_colimit_iff_lub`, so the vocabulary and the binary case come for free once that lands.

The pushout clause is a genuine increment, however, and it is not obviously inside this issue's current statement. The work scheduled here is about a *family* in a preorder — a discrete diagram — whereas a pushout is a colimit over a span; making the identification requires either stating the colimit result for an arbitrary index category (colimits in a thin category depend only on the set of objects of the diagram) or handling the span shape explicitly. Nothing in tree helps: the only two `HasPushouts` instances anywhere are `Instance/FinSet/Pushout.v:513` and `Instance/Sets/Pushout.v:185`, neither a thin category; `Instance/Proset.v:33` carries no colimit structure of any kind; and grepping `pushout` over `Instance/Poset.v`, `Instance/Proset.v`, `Instance/Props.v` and `Instance/Two.v` returns nothing.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §6.2.3) In a preorder's thin category, the colimit of an arbitrary diagram is the join of its objects — hence pushouts exist wherever binary joins do, and the pushout of any span coincides with the coproduct of its two feet.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §6.2.4 (printed p. 191; PDF p. 203; item `7sketches:6.2.4:def-finite-category`) fixes the same notion in an unnumbered footnote: a category is finite when it has finitely many morphisms. That is the finiteness predicate on an index category this issue schedules, and Seven Sketches uses it for exactly the reason Mac Lane does — to quantify "for every finite diagram".

The footnote adds one small observation that this issue's Definition of Done does not currently scope: such a category necessarily has finitely many *objects* too, since every object contributes its own identity morphism. That is a formalizable lemma and it is also the design hint for the predicate — the identification of objects with identity arrows is what makes an arrows-only presentation work.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §6.2.4) `finite_morphisms_implies_finite_objects` — a category with finitely many morphisms has finitely many objects, by the injection of objects into identity arrows.

On the `Theory/Metacategory` donor this issue names — **a Phase-D library defect the implementer must know about before leaning on it.** `Theory/Metacategory.v:157-158` defines `identity u := (∀ f : arr, composite f u f) /\ (∀ g : arr, composite u g g)` with **no definedness guard**, over `arr := nat`; since `pairs : M.t arr` is a finite map, no `u` can satisfy it. Hence `∃ i, identity M i` is provably empty and `FromArrows M` (`:261`) is the **empty category for every `M`**, including `Three := FromArrows ThreeArrows`. This is already proved in tree by the audit probe `doc/plan/books/probes/S8-metacategory-vacuity.v` (`identity_unsatisfiable`, `FromArrows_no_objects`, `Three_is_empty`), and the file's own comment at `:146-156` wrongly claims the guard-free encoding "is sound for the finite, explicitly-enumerated metacategories built here". What survives as a usable donor is the `Metacategory` record itself — `pairs : M.t arr` is genuine finite data, a category presented by a finite composition table — together with `cardinality` (`:415`) and `ThreeArrows_card_3` (`:447`), a syntactic count of identity entries that is independent of the broken predicate and does compute. The parallel `Theory/Metacategory/ArrowsOnly.v` keeps the conditional guard and is **not** vacuous; it is the healthier witness. Note also that `Metacategory` is declared inside `Module Metacategory (M : WSfun PNN)` (`:121`), never applied outside its own file, and its header at `:112-115` states that nothing in `Instance/`, `Construction/` or `Structure/` depends on it.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §6.2.4) Either repair `Theory/Metacategory.v:157-158`'s `identity` predicate with the definedness guard that `Theory/Metacategory/ArrowsOnly.v` already carries, or correct the false soundness claim at `:146-156` and redirect this issue's donor reference to `ArrowsOnly.v`.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §6.2.4, Definition 6.30 (printed p. 192; PDF p. 204; item `7sketches:6.2.4:def6.30`) defines the dual of what this issue defines: a category has finite colimits when every diagram over a finite index category has a colimit. It is blocked by exactly the same missing datum — with no finiteness predicate there is nothing to restrict the index category by — so it belongs here rather than in a separate definition issue.

The in-tree situation mirrors the limit side precisely. There is exactly one quantified colimit hypothesis, `Cocomplete` (`Structure/Complete.v:119`, `∀ (D : Category) (F : D ⟶ C), Colimit F`), which demands a colimit for *every* shape and so is strictly stronger than the book's property; `Structure/Complete.v:27-35` is explicit that the size discipline is carried implicitly by universe polymorphism rather than by any smallness datum. `Cocomplete` is instantiated nowhere — its only other occurrence is as a hypothesis in `Theory/Adamek/Corollaries.v:61`. Downstream consumers that actually want finite colimits take the shapes as separate hypotheses instead: `Construction/Cospan/Hypergraph.v:41` carries `Cocartesian C` + `Initial C` + `HasPushouts C` and calls that "finite colimits" in its header without ever forming the notion (a true statement of Borceux 2.8.2, so evidence of the gap rather than an error). The prose characterisation Definition 6.30 recalls — a colimit is an initial object in the category of cocones — is likewise proved only in its dual form, `Limit_Cones` (`Instance/Cones/Limit.v:37`), with the colimit direction left as a comment at `:34-36`, though `Cocones` itself does exist (`Instance/Cones.v:46`, `Cocones (F : J ⟶ C) := Cones (F^op)`).

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §6.2.4) `FinitelyCocomplete` defined over the same finiteness predicate, with covariant accessors, and the cocone characterisation `Colimit_Cocones : Initial (Cocones F) → Colimit F` stated rather than left as the comment at `Instance/Cones/Limit.v:34-36`.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §6.2.4, Example 6.42 (printed p. 194; PDF p. 206; item `7sketches:6.2.4:example6.42`) computes the coequalizer of `f, g : X → Y` in Set as the set of equivalence classes of `Y` under the relation generated by `y ~ y'` whenever some `x` has `f(x) = y` and `g(x) = y'`. That is exactly this issue's `Sets_HasCoequalizers` — "the coequalizer of `f`, `g` as the quotient of the codomain by the equivalence closure of `{f x ~ g x}`, the `pushout_eq` idiom of `Instance/Sets/Pushout.v` transposed" — so the construction is already scheduled here.

Two things are worth carrying across. First, the shape-and-universal-property half of the example is already in tree and is *stronger* than the book, which merely asserts the identification: `Coequalizer F := Colimit F` over `Parallel` (`Structure/Equalizer.v:126`) is reconciled with the elementary cofork property in **both** directions by `coequalizer_is_coequalizer` (`Structure/Coequalizer.v:226`) and `is_coequalizer_colimit` (`:275`), against `IsCoequalizer` (`:52`). So this issue is not re-proving anything about the shape — only supplying the concrete `Sets` object, which genuinely does not exist (`rg -i 'coequalizer' Instance/` returns exactly two hits, both prose comments at `Instance/Parallel.v:25` and `Instance/Two.v:51`).

Second, Seven Sketches uses the example for an application that has no in-tree counterpart and is a small, self-contained addition: taking `X` the set of "connect these two" markers and `Y` the set of ports of a circuit, the two families of arrows give functions `f, g : X → Y` whose coequalizer is the set of terminals resulting from the interconnection — the connected groups of ports.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §6.2.4) A worked `Sets` (or `FinSet`) coequalizer instance computing the interconnection of a small port set into its connected groups, so the construction has an evaluated witness and not only a universal property.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §6.3.3, Example 6.64 (printed p. 202; PDF pp. 214–215; item `7sketches:6.3.3:example6.64`) claims that the monoidal category of finite sets and corelations is a hypergraph category: every object `X` carries `μ_X : X ⊔ X → X` and `δ_X : X → X ⊔ X` (the corelation identifying exactly those elements arising from the same element of `X`), together with `η_X : ∅ → X` and `ε_X : X → ∅` (identifying nothing), and these form a special commutative Frobenius monoid. That is step 4 of this issue's work — "give the corelation category a hypergraph structure and hence, through `Hypergraph_CompactClosed`, a compact closed one" — and steps 1 and 3 supply the two prerequisites it needs (a concrete `CorelComposable` instance, since `CorelCat` is uninhabited in tree, and the transported symmetric monoidal structure). The stale in-tree assertions that a `CorelComposable Sets` instance already exists — `Instance/Sets/Pushout.v:41` and `:221` — are likewise already named in this issue's Definition of Done.

What Seven Sketches adds is the *explicit* Frobenius data and the compatibility clauses of its Definition 6.60. This issue's step 4 describes only the unit and counit ("the relation whose classes are the two copies of each element"), i.e. the cup and cap, whereas the hypergraph structure the example asserts is the full four-map supply on every object together with the monoidal-compatibility conditions — in the library's encoding, `Class Hypergraph` (`Structure/Monoidal/Hypergraph.v:144-173`) demands `scfa : ∀ X, SpecialCommutativeFrobenius X` plus four `scfa_tensor_*` and four `scfa_unit_*` coherences. As things stand nothing downstream of `Construction/Cospan/Corelation.v` exists at all: grepping `CorelCat`/`Corel_` outside that file returns zero hits, so there is no `Monoidal`, `SymmetricMonoidal`, Frobenius or `Hypergraph` instance on corelations of any kind.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §6.3.3) The four corelation Frobenius maps `μ_X`, `δ_X`, `η_X`, `ε_X` given explicitly in the book's form (identify exactly the elements coming from the same element of `X`; identify nothing), proved a `SpecialCommutativeFrobenius` on each object, and assembled into `@Hypergraph CorelCat _` with all eight tensor and unit coherence obligations discharged.
